question.prompt: When \(1999^{2000}\) is divided by \(5,\) the remainder is

solutions.explanation:
The ones digit of a product depends only on the ones digits of its factors, because all contributions from higher places are multiples of \(10\). Since \(9\cdot9=81\), the product \(1999\cdot1999\) ends in \(1\).

The \(2000\) factors of \(1999\) can be grouped into \(1000\) pairs. Every pair ends in \(1\), and multiplying numbers ending in \(1\) always gives another number ending in \(1\). Therefore \(1999^{2000}\) ends in \(1\).

Such a number is a multiple of \(10\) plus \(1\), so it is also a multiple of \(5\) plus \(1\). The remainder is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Pair factors and track the ones digit
